results.title: The 2026 Labor Market: What’s Ahead for Employers Through Year-End - Cascade Employers Association
results.content:
Recent Labor-Market Performance

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, nonfarm payroll employment increased by 162,000 in August, while the unemployment rate remained at 4.1%. The labor force participation rate edged up to 61.6%. Despite August's increase, average monthly employment growth over the previous 12 months was only 31,000, reflecting a substantially slower pace of job creation than employers experienced earlier in the recovery. [...] The Federal Reserve's September 2026 economic projections point to continued economic growth through 2026, with projected real GDP growth of 2.3% and an unemployment rate of 4.1%. At the same time, headline PCE inflation is projected at 3.7%, remaining meaningfully above the Federal Reserve's 2% longer-run goal. [...] The U.S. labor market is entering the final months of 2026 with a more measured pace of employment growth, while wage growth and inflation continue to influence employer decisions. August brought a stronger increase in payroll employment, but the broader picture remains one of slower and uneven growth across industries. For employers, this creates a balancing act for managing compensation and workforce costs while continuing to attract and retain the talent needed to meet organizational goals.

- Rob Haworth, senior investment strategy director with U.S. Bank Asset Management Group [...] “The September jobs report shows that hiring has slowed, but the labor market remains resilient,” says Rob Haworth, senior investment strategy director with U.S. Bank Asset Management Group. “Low unemployment, limited layoffs, and growing incomes give households a foundation for continued spending. We are watching whether those supports remain strong enough to offset higher food and energy prices.”

## Job openings and hiring show limited labor market movement [...] The September jobs report showed that U.S. hiring lost momentum after August’s rebound. Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, and the unemployment rate edged up to 4.2%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Employment changed little across major industries, reflecting the job market’s slower underlying trend.
